data = open('prices.db','rb').read()

#   offset 16: file change counter (4)
#   offset 20: db size in pages (4)
#   offset 24: first freelist trunk (4)
#   offset 28: freelist count (4)
#   offset 32: schema cookie (4)
#   offset 36: schema format (4)
#   offset 40: default page cache (4)
#   offset 44: largest root b-tree page (auto-vacuum) (4)
#   offset 48: text encoding (4)
#   offset 52: user version (4)
#   offset 56: incremental vacuum (4)
#   offset 60: application id (4)
#   offset 64: reserved for expansion (4)
#   offset 68: page type (1)  -- but for page 1 the b-tree header is at offset 100
# Actually for page 1, the b-tree page header starts at offset 100.
#   offset 100: page type (1): 0x0D = leaf table
#   offset 101: first freeblock (2)
#   offset 103: number of cells (2)
#   offset 105: cell content start (2)
#   offset 107: fragmented free bytes (1)
#   offset 108: right-most pointer (4) -- only for interior pages
#   offset 112: cell pointer array (2 bytes each)

# From the hex dump:

# offset 4 = 0x0A (num cells low) = 10 cells
# offset 5 = 0x0F (cell content start high)
# offset 6 = 0x3D (cell content start low) = 0x0F3D
# offset 7 = 0x00 (fragmented free bytes)
# offset 8..11: cell pointer 0 = 0x00000FF1? No wait.
# For a leaf page, there's no right-most pointer. So:
# offset 8: cell pointer 0 high
# offset 9: cell pointer 0 low
# ...

# Let me re-interpret:
# offset 0: 0x0D = page type (leaf table)
# offset 1-2: first freeblock = 0x0000
# offset 3-4: num cells = 0x000A = 10
# offset 5-6: cell content start = 0x0F3D
# offset 7: fragmented free bytes = 0x00
# offset 8-9: cell pointer 0
# offset 10-11: cell pointer 1
# ...

# From hex:
# offset 8: 0x0F, offset 9: 0xF1 -> cell 0 at 0x0FF1
# offset 10: 0x0F, offset 11: 0xE3 -> cell 1 at 0x0FE3
# offset 12: 0x0F, offset 13: 0xCB -> cell 2 at 0x0FCB
# offset 14: 0x0F, offset 15: 0xBD -> cell 3 at 0x0FBD
# offset 16: 0x0F, offset 17: 0xAD -> cell 4 at 0x0FAD
# offset 18: 0x0F, offset 19: 0x93 -> cell 5 at 0x0F93
# offset 20: 0x0F, offset 21: 0x7F -> cell 6 at 0x0F7F
# offset 22: 0x0F, offset 23: 0x6D -> cell 7 at 0x0F6D
# offset 24: 0x0F, offset 25: 0x58 -> cell 8 at 0x0F58
# offset 26: 0x0F, offset 27: 0x3D -> cell 9 at 0x0F3D

# So the cell pointers are at offsets 8..27 (10 pointers, 2 bytes each).
# This means the b-tree header starts at offset 0, not offset 100.
# That's unusual for page 1... unless the file was truncated and the
# first 100 bytes (the SQLite header) were cut off, leaving only the
# b-tree page header at what was originally offset 100.

# Actually wait. If the file was truncated from the FRONT (first 100 bytes
# removed), then what was originally at offset 100 is now at offset 0.
# The b-tree page header for a leaf table page is:
#   offset 0: page type (1)
#   offset 1-2: first freeblock (2)
#   offset 3-4: num cells (2)
#   offset 5-6: cell content start (2)
#   offset 7: fragmented free bytes (1)
#   offset 8: cell pointer array starts

# This matches perfectly! The file is the last 4096 bytes of a larger file,
# or the first 100 bytes were cut. Either way, we have a valid b-tree
# leaf page starting at offset 0.

print('num cells', num_cells)
